claim_handling_rules: Do not present synthesis notes as direct evidence.
Do not present metaphors as neuroscience.
Do not use exact statistics unless a verified source is attached.
Prefer student-safe paraphrases over clinical language.
Flag claims needing citation before public or grant-facing use.

initial_claims.claim: Procrastination may function as a self-protection strategy when performance is tied to worth.
initial_claims.student_safe_version: Sometimes avoiding a task is your brain trying to protect you from feeling judged.

initial_claims.claim: Students should ideate three parallel possible futures instead of searching for one perfect path.
initial_claims.student_safe_version: You do not need one perfect plan. You need multiple possible paths to test.

initial_claims.claim: Counting down 5-4-3-2-1 and moving can interrupt hesitation and help initiate action.
initial_claims.student_safe_version: When you know the next small action, count down and move before your brain argues you out of it.

initial_claims.claim: Conscious will is small compared with habits, conditioning, and environment.
initial_claims.student_safe_version: Your plans and your habits may be pulling in different directions.

initial_claims.claim: Environment and peer norms strongly shape behavior.
initial_claims.student_safe_version: It is easier to change when your surroundings support the change.
